The race condition could cause the persisted superblock checksum
to not match the contents of the superblock
superblock to be considered corrupt.
An example of the race follows.  A first thread is interrupted in the
middle of a checksum calculation. Then
superblock
thread resumes and sets the checksum based on the older superblock.
To fix
column2: serialize the superblock checksum calculation using the buffer

column1: header lock. While a spinlock is sufficient
already there and there is precedent for locking it (e.g. in
ext4_commit_super).
Tested the patch by booting up a kernel with the patch
a filesystem and some files (including some orphans)
unmounting and remounting the file system.
